name: Revenge runtime bundle
notes: The runtime that scripts/patch_runtime.py rewrites before it is published, and the only entry here that patch_runtime.py reads by name (its path ends in /revenge.js). It is not in this tree and its checksum is therefore not pinned: fetching it and recording the digest is the first step of restoring the Android build, and until that is done patch_runtime.py refuses to patch anything rather than patching an unreviewed upstream.

name: Storage hook patch text
source: this repository (the reviewed patch text patch_runtime.py splices into the runtime)
notes: patch_runtime.py reads this file and splices it in place of the runtime's own useProxy body; it is not in the tree, so the runtime patch step fails with a FileNotFoundError even after the upstream runtime has been fetched and pinned. This is a separate missing input from the runtime itself and belongs in the same commit.

name: Xposed API
notes: Every loader source imports de.robv.android.xposed.* (XposedBridge, XC_MethodHook, XposedHelpers, XC_LoadPackage), and the loader declares it compileOnly because the loaded process provides the classes at runtime. Resolved by Gradle from https://api.xposed.info/ (JCenter no longer serves it), so no staged file is needed and the path is empty on purpose.

name: Shared Android sources
source: this repository (the loader and the manager both import app.assault.shared.*)
notes: android/loader/.../AssaultLoader.java imports app.assault.shared.AccountSettings, and the manager imports it too. No android/shared module and no copy of these classes exists anywhere in the tree, so both modules currently fail to compile. settings.gradle deliberately does not declare the module: a module with no sources turns 'package app.assault.shared does not exist', which names the problem, into a Gradle error about an empty project. Add include ':android:shared' with the classes.

name: Command guide screen
notes: ManagerActivity builds a 'Command guide' button that calls CommandGuide; the class is imported and defined nowhere, so the manager does not compile.

name: Rich presence builder
notes: The manager's presence builder screen is built by RichPresence.show(this, preferences, onSaved), which is imported and defined nowhere.

name: Client download and patch engine
notes: The manager's whole engine and its largest missing piece. ManagerActivity uses CLIENT (the com.discord package id), installed(context), prepared(context), needsUpdate(context, version), beginPrepare(), prepareReserved(context, version, reporter), cancel(), clearDownloads(context), beginInstall(), verifyPrepared(context, files), busy, installing and progress. This is the app's own code - it cannot be substituted by a dependency or worked around in a build file.

name: Discord release feed
source: this repository (ManagerActivity and ScriptProvider reference it)
notes: ReleaseSource.latest() is what the manager checks against, ReleaseSource.copy(in, out) streams a prepared APK into the installer session, and ScriptProvider calls ReleaseSource.readBounded(in, 65536). Imported and defined nowhere.

name: Manager self-updater
notes: ManagerUpdater.prepared(context) returns the downloaded manager APK (its isFile() decides whether the install button is visible) and ManagerUpdater.check(context) performs the check. Imported and defined nowhere.

name: Install result receiver
source: this repository (declared in AndroidManifest.xml, started by ManagerActivity)
notes: The manifest declares <receiver android:name=".InstallReceiver"> and ManagerActivity fires an Intent for it with action app.assault.manager.INSTALL_RESULT. Absent from the tree, so the merged manifest points at a class that does not exist.

name: Update job service
source: this repository (declared in AndroidManifest.xml, scheduled by ManagerActivity)
notes: The manifest declares <service android:name=".UpdateJob" android:permission="android.permission.BIND_JOB_SERVICE"> and ManagerActivity schedules it with new JobInfo.Builder(26000, new ComponentName(context, UpdateJob.class)). Absent from the tree.

name: Addon file hand-off
source: this repository (AddonDocuments and ScriptDocuments call it)
notes: AddonFiles.publish(File, byte[]) is how the loader returns a result file to the manager: AddonDocuments publishes the addon request result and ScriptDocuments publishes a script run result. Absent from the tree, so the loader does not compile - and this is the bridge the addon browser depends on, so it is not cosmetic.

name: apkzlib
source: Google Maven: com.android.tools.build:apkzlib (the version has to be pinned deliberately)
notes: ApkPatcher.java imports com.android.tools.build.apkzlib.sign.SigningExtension/SigningOptions and zip.AlignmentRules/NestedZip/StoredEntry/ZFile/ZFileOptions to rewrite and re-sign the patched client. The library is published from Google's Maven repository under the com.android.tools.build group, but the version must match the rest of the toolchain, so the module declares a file dependency and leaves the line commented rather than pinning a version invented in this repository. Stage the jar here and uncomment implementation files('libs/apkzlib.jar').

name: ManifestEditor
source: WindySha's ManifestEditor (JitPack); the coordinate depends on the fork/commit
notes: ApkPatcher imports com.wind.meditor.core.ManifestEditor, property.AttributeItem, property.ModificationProperty and utils.NodeValue to rewrite the client manifest (package visibility and attributes) during patching. Not in the tree and not resolvable by a coordinate this repository can verify, so it is staged as a file: put it at this path and uncomment implementation files('libs/ManifestEditor.jar').

name: LSPatch share module
source: LSPatch (GPL-3.0) - its own :share module, not published to Maven under these packages
notes: ApkPatcher statically imports org.lsposed.lspatch.share.Constants fields (CONFIG_ASSET_PATH, EMBEDDED_MODULES_ASSET_PATH, LOADER_DEX_ASSET_PATH, ORIGINAL_APK_ASSET_PATH, PROXY_APP_COMPONENT_FACTORY) and uses Constants, LSPConfig and PatchConfig. Build the :share module from the LSPatch sources or take the classes from a release build; stage the jar here and uncomment implementation files('libs/lspatch-share.jar').

name: LSPatch patch module
source: LSPatch (GPL-3.0) - its own :patch module, not published to Maven under these packages
notes: ApkPatcher imports org.lsposed.patch.util.ApkSignatureHelper, Logger and ManifestParser. Stage the jar here and uncomment implementation files('libs/lspatch-patch.jar'). These classes are why the manager cannot be built from Maven alone.

name: Gson
notes: ApkPatcher.java imports com.google.gson.Gson for the patch config. Declared with a real, pinned version in android/manager/build.gradle and resolved by Gradle, so there is no staged file and the path is empty on purpose.

name: Apache Commons IO
notes: ApkPatcher.java imports org.apache.commons.io.FilenameUtils. Declared with a pinned version and resolved by Gradle, so no staged file is needed.

name: Manager resources
source: this repository (the manifest asks for two of them)
notes: There is no src/main/res in the manager module at all, and AndroidManifest.xml asks for @mipmap/ic_launcher (as both icon and roundIcon) and @xml/data_extraction_rules. The manifest merger fails on the first missing resource. Nothing in the module draws from XML - every screen is built programmatically - so an adaptive icon and the Android 12+ backup rules file are the entire requirement. The loader needs no res/ at all: its controls are framework widgets and it declares no theme or icon.

name: Loader manifest
notes: android/loader/src/main/ holds java/ and nothing else. An application module without a manifest does not build. It must declare package app.assault.loader and the Xposed entry points (xposedmodule / xposedminversion / xposeddescription meta-data) and nothing else - no activity, no launcher, no icon resource, because the module deliberately has no res/.

name: Xposed entry point asset
source: this repository (generated by the loader asset step)
notes: The file Xposed reads to find the entry point; its content must be exactly app.assault.loader.AssaultLoader. build_android.py refuses a bundle whose xposed_init says anything else, because a wrong class name here is an APK that loads nothing at all. Not in the tree.

name: Runtime bundle for the loader
notes: The patched Revenge runtime the loader injects (it is what hooks the client and builds the Addons, Themes and Code runner pages). Produced in step 8 of docs/android-build.md, which cannot run until the upstream runtime and the storage hook patch text both exist and the runtime's checksum is pinned. This is the asset the 16 MiB size cap is written for.

name: Capture asset
notes: One of the ten files the loader asset rules require and refuse to publish without. Its JS source has no home in this tree today, which is the missing assembly step: these assets are assembled into android/loader/src/main/assets/ before Gradle packages them.

name: Account controls asset
notes: Required by the loader asset rules (see the manager's Account controls screen for what it drives). Absent from the tree.

name: Rich presence asset
notes: Required by the loader asset rules. Absent from the tree.

name: History export asset
notes: Required by the loader asset rules. Absent from the tree.

name: HTML export asset
notes: Required by the loader asset rules. Absent from the tree.

name: Generated addon bundle
source: assembled from the JavaScript module roots (core/, utils/, plugins/, themes/)
notes: The bundle that carries the plugins and themes into the APK - it is the JavaScript half of the client (the addon manager and its screens in core/, the journal and validation in utils/, the sandbox and addon manager in plugins/, the theme tokens in themes/), and the patched runtime calls into it to build the Addons, Themes and Code runner pages. Nothing generates it today: the module-root assembly step is a missing input, and the loader asset rules refuse a bundle without it. Only this client's own addon dialect can run from it, so what ships as executable content is the bundled examples (plugins/examples/welcome.txt, themes/examples/amoled.txt); the 371-entry vendored catalogue is TypeScript metadata and is a separate, browse-only asset.

name: Acorn licence text
notes: Shipped inside the loader's asset bundle and required by the loader asset rules, so the build refuses a bundle without it. The licence text itself is not in this tree, which is why the licence files are listed as inputs rather than assumed.

name: Revenge licence text
notes: Shipped as licenses/Revenge-BSD-3-Clause.txt in the loader bundle and required by the same rules. The notice in the manager's open-source screen names this licence; the text itself is not in the tree.

name: Addon catalogue for the phone client
source: plugins/manifest.json, written by scripts/vendor.mjs from the Vencord and Equicord checkouts
notes: Not a compile input, so it does not block the build - but it is the asset that answers the owner's requirement that the APK carry the plugins and themes. The catalogue is metadata: those plugin bodies are TypeScript and this client's sandbox refuses them by design, so shipping the catalogue makes the entries browseable, not runnable. It also needs a reader: core/screens.js on the phone side has no catalogue source today, so the file can ship before the UI that lists it. Deliberately required: false so the CI gate does not claim it is a compile blocker.

name: Repository licence for the Android half
notes: There is no LICENSE at the repository root and none under android/, so the Android artifacts ship without a copy of the licence they are distributed under. Noted in README.md and docs/ANDROID-README.md as a gap; adding the text is a one-file change that nothing else depends on.

name: Code runner helper
notes: Present in the tree and shipped inside the manager. Its checksum is not pinned here yet: pinning is a step for whoever reviews the runner, and an unpinned file is reported as a gap by scripts/build_android.py rather than silently trusted.
